A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Boundary Guidance study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E in v2 and A–H in v3 are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and the appendices report original fine-tuning experiments across Qwen2.5 and Gemma models, including helpfulness, harmfulness, and ablation results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds classifier-score measurements, reward-only comparisons, reward-weight sensitivity, and PPO experiments.

M1.justification: The reward formulas, threshold, Algorithm 1, and guard-only and prompt-aware objectives remain unchanged. Appendix F adds an actual training-procedure variant: Qwen2.5-7B guard-only fine-tuning with PPO instead of GRPO. The main method continues to use GRPO.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same jailbreak collection, Alpaca, HarmfulQA, and HotpotQA coverage. The new analyses use retained models and prompt categories; permission gating and application examples are discussed but not evaluated as new tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds reward-model-only fine-tuning, R*=u, as an evaluated comparator against both full and guard-only Boundary Guidance across all four models (Tables 11–12). This supplies an important control for distinguishing boundary guidance from ordinary reward optimization that v2 lacked.

E3.justification: New experiments double the guard reward's relative weight and test PPO on Qwen2.5-7B. Table 2 also introduces the percentage of classifier scores outside [0.1, 0.9] as a diagnostic measure. The previously reported data composition, training budgets, and judge protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands mechanism and sensitivity testing: Table 2 checks whether scores become more extreme, Appendix D tests reward weighting, Appendix E isolates the contribution beyond reward-only training, and Appendix F tests optimizer dependence. The earlier prompt, classifier, judge, and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose a single training run in Appendix A.1 and retain the same paired t-test practices, task-prevalence weighting, and significance thresholds. The additional result tables do not introduce a new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds score-extremity proportions, mixed comparisons against reward-only training, and weight/PPO results. For example, Table 13 reports helpfulness/harmfulness of 2.68/0.16 under PPO versus 2.75/0.03 under GRPO. Matched earlier results are retained. However, new Table 10 lists original-weight harmfulness as 0.03, conflicting with 0.04 in retained Table 1.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces the assumption that utility is independent of the generation conditional on its score with a definition of score-conditional utility under a fixed generation policy. It also adds an explicit proof of Theorem 1. The theorem statement and Proposition 1's derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows 'improves both the safety and the utility' to improving safety while maintaining or improving utility. The conclusion also removes the assertion that pure boundary guidance drives larger-model improvements. The three principal contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets score extremes as evidence of successful boundary steering and discusses the new reward-only comparisons. Its Impact Statement adds potential information-access and auditability benefits. However, Section 5.2.1's claim that guard-only training matches or outperforms reward-only training overlooks the smallest model's helpfulness loss in Table 12. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Table 14 documents the PPO configuration, including KL coefficient 0.05, clip range 0.2, and value-function coefficient 0.1. The existing training configuration, hardware disclosure, evaluation prompts, and embedded code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Anthropic (2026) on Claude Code permission gating as another deployment example. Related-work positioning otherwise remains stable. Numerous reference changes update publication metadata; the two PPO entries in v3 refer to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted grammatical and terminology edits, updates affiliations and publication text, revises cross-references, and adds an Impact Statement and three appendix sections. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 10–14 add substantial new displays covering classifier-score extremes, reward-weight sensitivity, reward-only comparisons, and PPO results/configuration. Existing tables are rearranged and renumbered, and the ablation plot is resized within the revised layout. All three original figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The reward-only controls address an important omission in v2, while the score diagnostic, sensitivity experiments, and explicit theorem proof make the evidence easier to assess. The gain is limited by imperfect integration: Section 5.2.1 overstates guard-only superiority despite Table 12 showing helpfulness of 1.40 versus 2.38 for Qwen2.5-0.5B, and Table 10 conflicts with Table 1. Overall, the added controls improve assessability, but these reporting problems prevent a substantial quality improvement.
